scope: Bounded continuous numerical preservation for the retained runtime HDR controls optimization; no new production change.
interpretation: Every original, proxy, identity and enhanced payload matches the same prefix of the historical continuous reference. This extends prior fresh-cut controls to evolving model history without accepting the pre-existing reference as perceptually correct.
limitations: The fixed prefix spans 20 frames from one source and one setting; broad temporal/perceptual, source-rate Live, physical HDR and M5 acceptance remain open.

Automatic flow selection and private noise index are not directly observed. The same initial state, full prefix, code, inputs and model settings are preserved; outputs and public reset metadata compare exactly.
The full 56-frame input manifest is unchanged and preflighted. --frames20 limits output, so the original 6-GiB preflight ceiling is retained despite 1,990,656,000 actual payload bytes.

The 151.010-second process wall includes preflight and all capture work. The manifest 100.183-second elapsed value has a later origin. Post-process CPU comparisons are separate; none is an inference-throughput benchmark.
Unrelated Erika prototype source edits were in progress. The executed benchmark, its captured source map, model and runtime pins remained unchanged.
The standalone process uses a 256-MiB MLX cache policy; no parent-policy restoration or hard transient RSS guarantee is claimed.

limits: One persistent model, sequential processing and synchronous per-view readback/write
Specific cut/reset cause and selected automatic flow backend are unavailable in the public result
Stage wall timings include completed work; readback and disk overhead make this unsuitable as a throughput benchmark
Raw working references precede RGBA16F output packing and display mapping
No calibrated HDR, physical presentation, sustained A/V or temporal-quality qualification
